text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Residents in Medea, south of Algiers, experience a sort of uprising against armed groups following massacres of civilians in the city and threats to kill more among those backing the government security forces as well as rival faction.
- Ban on car stopping in Algiers main streets and squares eases clogged traffic. Residents have feeling that security may improve because the new traffic regulations help thwart car bomb attacks.
- The government adopts draft legislation to compensate victims of "terrorism".
- Criminal court sentences ex-Bouira province governor to one year in jail for graft.
- Noureddine Boukrouh, leader of the Algerian Renewal Party, urges opposition parties to abide by the law.
